lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Wesner! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to cook at home 4 nights?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 1 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to stop eating out so much.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm doing the best I can.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The days got away from you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is anyone else at home able to cook?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want your energy back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Easy for you to say.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to cook at home 4 nights.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 6. Maybe 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 6 and not a 3?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 1 out of 4 days, the hard part was finding the time, and next week you're going to cook at home 4 nights. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Tuesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

flags.reason: Directive 'You have to stop eating out' right after participant's grandkids motivation; missed change talk.
'You have to make this a priority' pushes without permission; participant pushed back at line 30.
Goal set by coach ('I want you to') without asking participant or collaborating; participant hesitant.
Coach cites 5 days, but the agreed goal discussed was 4 nights; confusing the participant.

score.summary: The coach used some useful reflections and a good confidence-ruler and barrier-planning sequence that drew out the participant's own plan. However, several directive statements ('You have to...', 'I want you to') and a misstated goal (5 days vs. 4 nights) undermined partnership and missed the participant's change talk about grandkids.
strengths: Line 33 complex reflection captured participant's ambivalence about starting small and sticking with it.
Line 39-41 open questions after the confidence rating elicited the participant's own plan (line 40, 42).
Line 43 summary clearly recapped the plan and checked for anything missed.
coaching_tips: Line 11 and 29: replace directives with reflection, e.g., 'It sounds like your grandkids matter a lot to you, what would help you cook more?'
Line 35: ask permission and offer collaboration before setting the next-week goal, e.g., 'Would you be open to trying 4 nights next week? What feels doable?'
Line 27: double-check the agreed goal before asking; the discussion was about 4 nights, not 5.
Line 10: when participant names grandkids and avoiding dad's path, explore that change talk further with an open question.
